summary: Spot 1 is most consistent with a monolayer (1L). Its E2g1–A1g separation is 62.01 cm-1, which matches the 1L value of 62.0 cm-1 in Berkdemir et al. 2013 Table 1, and it is the only layer label within ±0.3 cm-1. Its 2LA(M)/A1g height ratio of 2.2 is also in the range the same source gives for 1L at 514.5 nm. Spot 2 has Δ = 64.70 cm-1, which is 3L or bulk (the relation cannot separate them). The 1L call rests on one reference table; cross-group offsets of about 1.7 cm-1 in Δ exist (Hait 2022), so an independent check (AFM step height or PL) is needed before calling it certain. The relative result is more robust than the absolute one: between spots, A1g stiffens by +2.9 cm-1 and Δ widens by +2.7 cm-1, the same as the 1L→bulk change in that table, while E2g1 barely moves. The 2LA–A1g separation (65.6 and 67.0 cm-1 from the series tool) is not the E2g–A1g separation and must not be used for layer number.

observations.finding: Peak assignment (both spots, 514.5 nm, 295 K, Si-corrected): 175 cm-1 LA(M); 350.9 (spot 1) and 349.8 (spot 2) cm-1 2LA(M); 355.1 (spot 1) and 355.3 (spot 2) cm-1 E2g1; 417.1 (spot 1) and 420.0 (spot 2) cm-1 A1g; 520.8 cm-1 Si substrate.
observations.evidence: Two-Lorentzian joint fit of 335-372 cm-1 (spot 1: 2LA 350.861 +- 0.065, FWHM 8.87; E2g1 355.057 +- 0.076, FWHM 4.03; spot 2: 2LA 349.786 +- 0.138; E2g1 355.294 +- 0.044). A1g from single Lorentzian on 405-432 cm-1 (spot 1 417.073 +- 0.026, FWHM 4.53; spot 2 419.985 +- 0.014, FWHM 4.37). Si offsets +0.21 (spot 1) and +0.09 (spot 2) cm-1 subtracted. Reference positions: Berkdemir Table 1 at 514.5 nm: 1L 351.1 / 355.2 / 417.2; bulk 350.0 / 355.3 / 420.1.
observations.source: Labels and 1L/bulk reference positions: Berkdemir et al. 2013, Sci. Rep. 3, 1755, Table 1 (doi:10.1038/srep01755)

observations.finding: The 2LA(M) and E2g1 components must be fitted jointly; the library tool's default single-peak fit misassigns them. A single Lorentzian at 351.7 cm-1 (FWHM 9.9) leaves a clear residual at about 355 cm-1 and a baseline offset, while the two-component model is strongly preferred.
observations.evidence: Spot 1: AIC 407.5 (1 peak) vs 293.2 (2 peaks), delta AIC 114.3; chi2 8.5e4 -> 9.2e3. Spot 2: AIC 488.6 vs 322.7, delta AIC 165.8. The rl_fit default output for spot 1 (window 330-380) returned one band at 351.7 with FWHM 9.9.
observations.source: Mitioglu et al. 2014, PRB 89, 245442 (arXiv:1406.3511, abstract): a single-Lorentzian fit of the 2LA/E2g doublet misplaces E2g1 and can give a wrong layer number; WS2 note in the skill

observations.finding: The series tool's 'two strongest separation' values (65.6 cm-1 spot 1; 67.0 cm-1 spot 2) are the 2LA(M)–A1g separation, not the E2g1–A1g separation used for layer number. Using them would wrongly push spot 1 toward multilayer.
observations.source: Mitioglu 2014 abstract and Berkdemir 2013 Table 1 (E2g1 and A1g are the layer-sensitive pair)

observations.finding: Spot 1 is 1L under the layer-separation relation (high confidence, single candidate). Spot 2 is 3L or bulk (low confidence; relation cannot separate them).
observations.evidence: ws2_layer_number_from_separation: spot 1 Δ = 62.01 cm-1 with delta_err 0.3 gives candidates ['1L'] (2L at 63.4 is outside the uncertainty). Spot 2 Δ = 64.70 gives candidates ['3L','bulk'] (3L 64.6, bulk 64.8). Relation validity: Δ 61-66 cm-1, laser 488-647 nm; 514.5 nm inside.
observations.source: Berkdemir et al. 2013, Sci. Rep. 3, 1755, Table 1 (doi:10.1038/srep01755); Mitioglu 2014 (arXiv:1406.3511, p.2) gives Δ from about 62 (1L) to 66 (bulk)

observations.finding: The spot 1 to spot 2 shift pattern is thickness-like: A1g stiffens by +2.92 cm-1 while E2g1 changes by only +0.23 cm-1 and 2LA(M) softens by -1.07 cm-1. The change in Δ (+2.69) matches the 1L-to-bulk change in the same reference table (62.0 to 64.8).
observations.evidence: Fit errors: A1g +/-0.03 and +/-0.01 cm-1; E2g1 +/-0.08 and +/-0.04; 2LA +/-0.07 and +/-0.14. Si-offset difference between spots is 0.12 cm-1 and the calibration budget is a few tenths of a cm-1, so the A1g shift is significant and the E2g1 shift is not. A1g FWHM is unchanged (4.53 vs 4.37 cm-1), so no broadening signal accompanies it.
observations.source: Berkdemir 2013 Table 1 (A1g 417.2 to 420.1, E2g1 355.2 to 355.3, 1L to bulk at 514.5 nm); WS2 note: A1g stiffens with N while E2g1 barely moves (Berkdemir 2013, Table 1, consensus)

observations.finding: Intensity ratios point the same way: 2LA(M)/A1g height ratio is 2.23 in spot 1 and 0.47 in spot 2; 2LA(M)/E2g1 is 4.2 and 0.80. The 2LA(M) band dominates in the 1L-like spot, consistent with resonant enhancement at 514.5 nm.
observations.evidence: Heights from the two-component fit: spot 1 2LA 1792, E2g1 429, A1g 805; spot 2 2LA 531, E2g1 666, A1g 1131 (counts after ALS-free local linear background).
observations.source: Berkdemir 2013 (2LA/A1g about 2 at 514 nm for 1L, decreasing with N, as relayed in the WS2 note, Fig. 3); Yang et al. 2017 arXiv:1706.01677 p.5 (2LA stronger than main peaks at 2.33 and 2.41 eV)

observations.finding: The LA(M) band near 175 cm-1 is present in both spots. Relative to A1g it is stronger in spot 1 (0.14) than in spot 2 (0.04). Its presence is not a defect marker for WS2 near resonance.
observations.evidence: rl_series: 175.68 cm-1 (height 111, FWHM 9.3) spot 1; 175.21 cm-1 (height 49, FWHM 10.2) spot 2 (+/-0.6, weak). Height ratios to A1g: 0.14 and 0.04.
observations.source: Berkdemir 2013 (LA(M) near 176 at 488 nm); Zhang X. et al. 2015, Chem. Soc. Rev. 44, 2757 (arXiv:1502.00701) Table III (zone-edge combinations at 176, 193, 231 cm-1)

observations.finding: Bands at 297 (E1g, backscattering-forbidden), 310 (multilayer-only marker) and 325 cm-1 (E2g2+LA) were not detected above the SNR-2 threshold in either spot. The 193 and 231 cm-1 bands were also absent in spot 1. The 310 cm-1 band's absence is consistent with 1L, but is not a proof.
observations.evidence: rl_fit --min-snr 2 for both spots: no bands between 282.6 and 349.9 cm-1 except the 2LA band; the narrow features at 266 and 283 cm-1 (FWHM about 1 cm-1 at a single point) are at the resolution limit and are not claimed.
observations.source: Zhao W. et al. 2013, Nanoscale 5, 9677 (arXiv:1304.0911, p.10, Fig. 5b): 310 cm-1 present in multilayers and absent in 1L; Kumar D. et al. 2019 J. Phys.: Condens. Matter (doi:10.1088/1361-648X/ab3fec, abstract): 297 cm-1 is E1g, 325 cm-1 is E2g2+LA (disputed in Hait 2022 p.4)

observations.finding: Calibration: the Si line sits at 520.91 cm-1 (spot 1) and 520.78 cm-1 (spot 2) by QC, offsets +0.21 and +0.08 cm-1 from 520.7. The Δ separation is independent of a rigid calibration shift; absolute positions carry about a few tenths of a cm-1 systematic error.
observations.evidence: rl_qc output; series Si offsets 0.21 and 0.09 cm-1 subtracted before fitting; Δ unchanged by a common shift.
observations.source: Castellanos-Gomez et al. 2014 (arXiv:1403.0499, p.7, Si first order 520.9 cm-1); WS2 note and artifacts note on calibration

properties.name: layers
properties.value: spot 1: 1 (1L); spot 2: 3L or bulk (not separable; low confidence)
properties.source: ws2_layer_number_from_separation relation; Berkdemir et al. 2013, Sci. Rep. 3, 1755, Table 1 (doi:10.1038/srep01755)

properties.name: phase
properties.value: 2H (as stated by the user; not independently tested here, though the 1T/1T' distinction in Kumar 2019 is not tested in this window)
properties.source: User statement; Kumar D. et al. 2019 J. Phys.: Condens. Matter (doi:10.1088/1361-648X/ab3fec, abstract) on 1T vs 2H spectra

properties.source: E2g1 shift between spots +0.23 cm-1 (not significant given calibration budget); strain would shift E2g1 with A1g (WS2 note, Dadgar et al. 2018, Chem. Mater., doi:10.1021/acs.chemmater.8b01672)

properties.name: doping_type
properties.source: A1g FWHM unchanged between spots (4.53 vs 4.37 cm-1); no WS2-specific doping rate verified (WS2 note; Chakraborty 2012 used only by analogy)

properties.name: defect_level
properties.source: No WS2-specific defect calibration verified in the skill notes; LA(M) presence is not a defect marker near resonance (WS2 note, Berkdemir 2013)

caveats: The 1L call depends on the Berkdemir 2013 Table 1 reference scale. Hait et al. 2022 (J. Appl. Phys. 132, 133901, p.4) gives 1L positions of 353.98 / 357.97 / 418.23 cm-1, i.e. Δ about 60.3 cm-1 (cross-group offset of about 1.7 cm-1). On that scale spot 1 would not sit on 1L. The relative spot 1 vs spot 2 result (Δ +2.7 cm-1) does not depend on this scale.

The 2L candidate sits only 1.4 cm-1 from spot 1's Δ in the same reference table (2L 63.4). With a 0.3 cm-1 uncertainty it is excluded, but any systematic difference of about 1 cm-1 between fitting models or groups would reopen it. The rl_fit single-peak output and the series separation are both wrong for this (see observations).

2LA/A1g and 2LA/E2g height ratios depend on the polarization geometry (Mitioglu 2014 p.4, Fig. 3; Yang 2017 p.5). Polarization was not given, so the ratios are supporting evidence only. The 2L value of the 2LA/A1g ratio is not tabulated in the skill notes, so the ratio cannot be used to exclude 2L.

Substrate interference on SiO2/Si changes absolute intensities (Yoon et al. 2009, PRB 80, 125422, as relayed in artifacts.md). Both spots share the same SiO2/Si stack, but absolute heights and Si ratios were not used for thickness.

Two-component fit: my own check (lmfit Lorentzians with a local linear background over 335-372 cm-1), not the skill's rl_fit. It is saved at C:/WINDOWS/TEMP/ws2-check/doublet_fit.py. I did not plot its residual; the evidence is the AIC and chi2 improvement. Fit-only errors are 0.03 to 0.2 cm-1; a Voigt or fixed-width model could shift the E2g1 centre by a few tenths of a cm-1 (not tested).

Laser heating: the differential temperature coefficient of Δ is small (Huang et al., Sci. Rep. 2016, as relayed in artifacts.md: E -0.0093 and A1g -0.0122 cm-1/K for 1L, a difference of about 0.003 cm-1/K), so Δ is insensitive to heating over tens of K. Absolute positions would shift by about 0.3 to 0.4 cm-1 for 30 K. Laser power was not given, so heating was not estimated.

The spectral resolution was not reported and rl_qc does not compute it. The E2g1 and A1g FWHMs (4.0 to 4.5 cm-1) may be partly instrument-limited (Das et al. 2008; Zhang et al. 2013 per the artifacts note), so no width-based conclusion is drawn.

The library matcher's top DFT candidate is S2W (R3m, a 3R-type WS2 entry from the Computational Raman Database), with no literature candidate returned. I kept the user's 2H label. The 2H vs 3R polytype was not discriminated in this window, though E2g1 and A1g are the same symmetry labels in both.

The 297 E1g and 325 E2g2+LA bands were not seen at SNR 2. The 310 cm-1 band is absent in both spots; this agrees with 1L (Zhao et al. 2013) but is not a proof, because its assignment is unclear in the source and the detection threshold may hide weak bands.
questions_for_user: Is there an AFM step height or photoluminescence (A exciton) measurement on spot 1? A PL map is the most direct check for a monolayer, and AFM would settle the thickness independently of the Raman reference scale.
What laser power at the sample and spot size were used? Power matters for heating, and the absolute intensities cannot be used without it.

What was the polarization geometry (unpolarized, parallel or crossed; analyzer present)? The 2LA/A1g and 2LA/E2g ratios depend on it, so they cannot be compared with the 514.5 nm references without this.
What is the spectral resolution, grating and calibration date? This sets the instrument-limited width floor and the calibration uncertainty for the absolute positions.
Is the SiO2 thickness known and the same under spot 1 and spot 2? Interference changes absolute intensities.

Was a low-frequency (shear/breathing) measurement made with a notch or ultra-low-frequency filter? That would give an independent layer test; the current data start at 120 cm-1, so shear and breathing modes are not accessible here.
Has the 2H polytype been confirmed independently (for example by SHG or TEM)? The library's top DFT match is a 3R-type entry and the polytype was not discriminated here.

limits: Not measured here: AFM step height, photoluminescence, polarization geometry, laser power, spot size, spectral resolution, and low-frequency shear/breathing modes below 120 cm-1. The thickness conclusion therefore rests on Raman alone.

Only one relation was applied quantitatively: the E2g1–A1g layer-separation relation (ws2_layer_number_from_separation), valid for 61-66 cm-1 and 488-647 nm. It was used with delta_err 0.3 cm-1; the default 0.5 cm-1 also gives the same spot 1 result (1L only).
Heating and power-density effects, substrate interference (SiO2 thickness not given), and temperature-dependent shifts beyond the 295 K stated were not quantified; no laser power was supplied.

The two-component doublet fit is my own check and was not validated against a reference fit of the same spectra. Its errors are fit statistics only; systematic differences of a few tenths of a cm-1 are possible.
The 2L and 3L/bulk candidates were not separated by any relation or intensity ratio available in the skill notes. A 2L-specific 2LA/A1g ratio is not tabulated there.
Monolayer thickness (~0.7 nm) is general knowledge and was not taken from the skill's sources; treat it as an assumption to be checked by AFM.
